selected_evidence.requirement: Service inventory-worker created, managed by systemd, running as long-lived background worker
selected_evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now succeeded; status shows Active: running with worker process and sleep child; is-enabled/is-active both confirm managed service state
As inventory-worker: write to /etc/should-fail returned Permission denied (exit=1); write to /var/lib/inventory/should-work succeeded (exit=0), directly proving the write confinement
grep NoNewPrivs /proc/$MainPID/status returned NoNewPrivs: 1 for the running service process

selected_evidence.requirement: Worker is long-running and actively producing data
selected_evidence.summary: worker.log shows incrementing timestamped ticks before and after restart, proving continuous operation
Captured boot_id 4a743885-c59f-43ee-afde-ef96f7bea723, uptime since 09:43:10, service active, and log ticks 1-3 prior to reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded self-delayed systemctl reboot; exec call returned 'reboot-scheduled' immediately, ack received before the node went down

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart)
selected_evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 4a743885-c59f-43ee-afde-ef96f7bea723 to a8869031-5516-4307-bbae-318914d30051; connection failures observed mid-reboot; uptime reset to 09:44:03 confirming a real reboot occurred

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 service and data recovered post-restart
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart: service enabled+active with new MainPID 738 (previously 1307), worker.log continued appending new ticks while retaining pre-restart entries, confirming both service and data recovery

commands.command: useradd -r -s /sbin/nologin -d /var/lib/inventory inventory-worker 2>&1; mkdir -p /var/lib/inventory; chown inventory-worker:inventory-worker /var/lib/inventory; chmod 750 /var/lib/inventory; id inventory-worker

cat > /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
DATA_DIR=/var/lib/inventory
LOG_FILE="$DATA_DIR/worker.log"
i=0
while true; do
  i=$((i+1))
  ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  printf '%s tick=%s pid=%s\n' "$ts" "$i" "$$" >> "$LOG_FILE"
  sleep 10
done
EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh
cat /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh

commands.command:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Inventory worker (sandboxed)
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=inventory-worker
Group=inventory-worker
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh
Restart=on-failure

NoNewPrivileges=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory
ReadOnlyPaths=/usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh
StateDirectory=inventory
StateDirectoryMode=0750

PrivateDevices=yes
ProtectKernelTunables=yes
ProtectKernelModules=yes
ProtectKernelLogs=yes
ProtectControlGroups=yes
ProtectClock=yes
ProtectHostname=yes
RestrictSUIDSGID=yes
RestrictRealtime=yes
RestrictNamespaces=yes
LockPersonality=yes
MemoryDenyWriteExecute=yes
CapabilityBoundingSet=
AmbientCapabilities=
SystemCallFilter=@system-service
SystemCallErrorNumber=EPERM

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now inventory-worker
sleep 2
systemctl status inventory-worker --no-pager -l
